title: Triglyceride Metabolism
objectives: Understand the structure and biological significance of triglycerides
Describe the pathways of triglyceride synthesis (lipogenesis) and breakdown (lipolysis)
Explain the regulation of triglyceride metabolism in fed and fasted states
Analyze the role of triglycerides in energy homeostasis
Identify clinical disorders related to triglyceride metabolism

overview.title: Triglyceride Overview
overview.content:
Triglycerides (TGs), or triacylglycerols, are the main storage form of lipids in the body, consisting of a glycerol backbone esterified with three fatty acids. They serve as the body's most concentrated energy source, providing 9 kcal/g, and are stored in adipose tissue lipid droplets.

Biological Significance

  • Energy Reservoir: Major form of stored energy (~100,000 kcal in average adult)
  • Insulation: Subcutaneous fat provides thermal insulation
  • Organ Protection: Visceral fat cushions internal organs
  • Metabolic Water: Oxidation yields metabolic water (important for desert animals)

Structural Features

Components

  • Glycerol (3-carbon alcohol)
  • 3 Fatty acids (saturated/unsaturated)
  • Ester bonds (between -OH and -COOH)

Properties

  • Hydrophobic (water-insoluble)
  • Less oxidized than carbohydrates (more energy/gram)
  • Stored in anhydrous form (compact energy)

synthesis.title: Triglyceride Synthesis (Lipogenesis)
synthesis.content:
Glycerol-3-Phosphate Pathway

Location: Liver and adipose tissue cytoplasm

Precursors: Glycerol-3-P (from glucose or glycerol), fatty acyl-CoAs

Key Enzymes: GPAT, AGPAT, lipin, DGAT

Biochemical Steps

  1. Glycerol-3-P + fatty acyl-CoA → Lysophosphatidic acid (GPAT)
  2. Lysophosphatidic acid + fatty acyl-CoA → Phosphatidic acid (AGPAT)
  3. Phosphatidic acid → Diacylglycerol (lipin/PAP enzyme)
  4. Diacylglycerol + fatty acyl-CoA → Triglyceride (DGAT)

Regulation

Activators: Insulin, carbohydrate-rich diet (via SREBP-1c)

Inhibitors: Glucagon, epinephrine, fasting (via AMPK)

breakdown.title: Triglyceride Breakdown (Lipolysis)
breakdown.content:
Hormone-Sensitive Lipase Pathway

Location: Adipocyte lipid droplets

Hormonal Control: Catecholamines (activate), insulin (inhibits)

Key Enzymes: ATGL, HSL, MGL

Stepwise Hydrolysis

  1. TG → DG + FFA (adipose triglyceride lipase, ATGL)
  2. DG → MG + FFA (hormone-sensitive lipase, HSL)
  3. MG → glycerol + FFA (monoacylglycerol lipase, MGL)

Fatty Acid Mobilization

FFA Transport: Bound to albumin in circulation

Glycerol Fate: Liver gluconeogenesis or glycolysis

Energy Yield: Complete oxidation of palmitate → 106 ATP

transport.title: Triglyceride Transport
transport.content:
Chylomicrons

Origin: Intestinal enterocytes

Function: Transport dietary TGs to tissues via lymphatics

Key Apoproteins: B-48, C-II, E

VLDL

Origin: Liver hepatocytes

Function: Transport endogenous TGs to peripheral tissues

Key Apoproteins: B-100, C-II, E

Lipoprotein Lipase (LPL)

Location: Capillary endothelial surfaces

Function: Hydrolyzes TG core of lipoproteins

Regulation: Activated by apo C-II, inhibited by apo C-III

clinical_correlations.title: Clinical Correlations
clinical_correlations.content:
Hypertriglyceridemia

Causes: Insulin resistance, genetic disorders (LPL deficiency), alcohol

Risks: Pancreatitis (>1000 mg/dL), cardiovascular disease

Lipodystrophies

Types: Congenital (e.g., Berardinelli-Seip) vs acquired (HIV-related)

Features: Fat loss, severe insulin resistance, hypertriglyceridemia

Therapeutic Targets

Fibrates: PPARα agonists that enhance LPL activity

Omega-3 Fatty Acids: Reduce hepatic VLDL production

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why can't triglycerides cross cell membranes directly?+
Their large size and extreme hydrophobicity require specialized transport via lipoproteins (chylomicrons/VLDL) and breakdown by lipases at tissue sites.
How does insulin simultaneously promote TG storage and inhibit breakdown?+
Insulin activates lipoprotein lipase (increasing TG uptake) while inhibiting HSL via phosphatase-mediated dephosphorylation, creating coordinated anabolic signaling.
What prevents continuous cycling between TG synthesis and breakdown?+
Compartmentalization (synthesis in ER, breakdown in lipid droplets) and reciprocal regulation by insulin (storage) vs catecholamines (mobilization).
Why are medium-chain triglycerides (MCTs) metabolized differently?+
MCTs (6-12 carbons) are absorbed directly into portal blood and don't require chylomicron formation, making them rapid energy sources that bypass normal TG processing.
